title: Quarter Synchronization Hub for Company OKRs and Cross-functional Dependencies
creator: Daniel Ortiz
description: Create a lightweight, repeatable Quarter Synchronization Hub (QSH) that standardizes how company-level OKRs are decomposed into cross-functional initiatives, surfaces inter-team dependencies, and provides a single source of truth for roadmap sequencing and trade-offs. The hub is intended to reduce misalignment between Product, Engineering, Design, and GTM by providing an intake, weekly triage, dependency map, and a decision log for the quarter. Scope: company-level OKRs and initiatives for the upcoming quarter, handoffs into team-level cycles, and a mechanism for handling mid-quarter emergency scope shifts.
acceptance_criteria: QSH template (Confluence) published with mandated fields for initiative intent, success metrics, owners, dependencies, and rollout plan
Weekly QSH triage meeting cadence established, calendar invites and owners assigned
Dependency map (shared Miro) created for top 12 initiatives and linked to each initiative page
Two pilot initiatives moved through QSH with documented decisions and updated team roadmaps
Dashboards that show initiative progress vs OKR target available in Console (links in 'links' field)
updates: 2025-02-14: Kickoff with PM, Eng leads, and Design. Agreed scope and initial stakeholder list. Action: Priya to draft Confluence template by 2025-02-18.

2025-02-18: First draft of QSH template posted: https://confluence.internal.redwood/qsh/template (PR for template comments: https://github.com/redwood/product/pulls/402). Feedback requested from Eng infra and Reliability teams.
2025-02-20: Pilot candidates chosen (Dedicated autoscale policy workstream, Console rollout for cost breakdowns). Miro board created: https://miro.com/app/board/uXQ-QuarterSync/ .

2025-02-23: Lightweight dependency mapping exercise with Eng (kernel selection), Infra (Dedicated capacity), and Console. Identified three critical dependencies: KV cache improvement (ENG-2101), rollout API contract (ENG-2199), and billing schema change (FIN-77).
2025-02-26: Weekly triage scheduled Fridays 10am PST. Priya to run first runbook and collect initiative owners. Will capture decisions in the QSH decision log.
decisions: Adopt two-tier initiative classification: Strategic (direct OKR contributor) vs Enabler (supports multiple strategic initiatives). This reduces triage overhead during weekly sync.
Use Confluence QSH template as the canonical artifact for initiative intent and OKR mapping. Short-term: link initiative pages from the company OKR dashboard.

For mid-quarter emergency scope shifts, support a 'fast-track' approval path: emergency triage + fallback routing to alternate model variant. Fast-track requires signoff from PM + Eng lead + Head of Product.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Risk: Adding another process creates overhead; mitigated by limiting weekly sync to 45 minutes and enforcing a strict agenda.
Tradeoff: Centralized decision log improves visibility but can slow down team autonomy; will allow teams to opt-out for low-risk enablers.
Risk: Dependency mapping accuracy depends on timely updates from teams; mitigation: owners will be required to update the Miro map before each sync and failure will escalate to program manager.
